Title: May 28, 2026 - City of Boulder City Council Special Meeting and Study Session
Overview: Council unanimously endorsed Councilmember Matt Benjamin's nomination to the Colorado Municipal League Executive Board and unanimously approved Ordinance 8749 authorizing property acquisition, including eminent domain as a last resort, for the Arapahoe Avenue safety project. Council voted 5-3 to direct staff to research two airport land-use options and schedule a public hearing, then gave staff direction to draft DDA formation ballot measures for a November 2026 vote after discussing financial structure, parking transfers, and general fund impacts.

Topic1.Title: Consent Agenda: CML Executive Board Nomination
Topic1.Summary: Council added item 2A to the consent agenda to confirm its endorsement of Councilmember Matt Benjamin's nomination to the Colorado Municipal League Executive Board. Benjamin explained that Boulder holds two CML appointments and that the executive board sets CML's policy positions on state legislation. The consent agenda passed 8-0 with Benjamin recused.

Topic2.Title: Ordinance 8749: Arapahoe Avenue Right-of-Way Acquisition
Topic2.Summary: Staff presented the East Arapahoe (CO 7) safety project, funded by a federal grant with $2.4 million in city match for a $12 million total, which requires temporary and permanent easements on 14 properties averaging about 700 square feet each. Staff said the eminent domain authority is needed to avoid schedule delays that could jeopardize the federal spending deadline in 2030, and that negotiation is expected to succeed. Council asked about property owner protections and budget placeholders, and one member of the public spoke in opposition. Council then unanimously approved Ordinance 8749.

Topic3.Title: Airport Land Use: Public Hearing and Research Direction
Topic3.Summary: Staff presented scenario A, keeping the airport open indefinitely, and asked council whether to act by consent agenda or public hearing on a motion affirming continued airport use. Most council members favored a public hearing given community interest, and eight members raised hands for that option. Council then debated whether legal research on long-term land encumbrance and FAA grant implications should be done before a hearing, and five members voted to direct staff to bring back two options. Staff said the research would take time and that the budget process is a key pressure point.

Topic4.Title: DDA Formation: Plan of Development and Investment Priorities
Topic4.Summary: Staff introduced a proposed Downtown Development Authority to reinvest in downtown and University Hill, citing flat downtown sales tax since 2020 and aging GID parking assets. The draft plan of development sets a 30-year framework with five priority areas: strategic site redevelopment, commercial corridor health, mixed-use development, public space investment, and connectivity. Staff stressed that the plan is a legal framework rather than a binding project commitment and that council approves the plan and budgets.

Topic5.Title: DDA Financial Structure: TIF, Mill Levy, and Parking Assets
Topic5.Summary: The proposed financing combines tax increment financing, a 3.674 mill levy replacing existing GID levies, and parking asset integration. Staff projected about $1.8 million per year from the mill levy and roughly $18 to $26 million in cumulative six-year revenue across sources. Property tax TIF would capture about half of new growth within the boundary, while sales tax TIF captures growth above a 12-month baseline. Staff acknowledged that the financial impact on the general fund and other taxing entities still needs more analysis.

Topic6.Title: DDA Governance, Ballot Measures, and Timeline
Topic6.Summary: Council would appoint the DDA board, approve the annual budget and plan amendments, and set terms of an intergovernmental agreement covering revenue sharing and parking asset transfers. Staff proposed three November 2026 ballot questions covering DDA formation, the mill levy, and TIF authorization, with a draft IGA returning August 6. Qualified electors include property owners, residents, and business lessees within the boundary, with an estimated 2,500 eligible electors. The timeline includes board formation and plan adoption around spring 2027 if approved.

Topic7.Title: Council Questions and Feedback on DDA Proposal
Topic7.Summary: Council questioned how the DDA would affect general fund sales tax, school and library district property tax, parking rate authority, and measurement of economic outcomes. Members raised equity concerns that University Hill investment might be subordinated to downtown and asked for clearer accountability metrics and parking governance guardrails. Council members generally supported moving toward ballot measures while asking for more financial analysis before final decisions. Staff agreed to provide additional information on general fund impacts, parking asset sale proceeds, and draft IGA terms.

Topic8.Title: DDA Direction Vote and Study Session Close
Topic8.Summary: Council provided direction on the draft plan, the financial structure, and staff drafting ballot measures for November 2026. Most members expressed support for moving forward, with some conditioning approval on more financial information. Staff confirmed they had enough direction to proceed and invited follow-up questions by email. The study session ended shortly after 8:30 p.m.
